name: CEPI (Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations)
summary: A Norwegian non-profit association, founded in 2017 and based in Oslo with offices in London and Washington, DC, that funds the development of vaccines against epidemic and pandemic threats: rapid-response vaccine platforms and libraries for an unknown 'Disease X', vaccines against Lassa, Nipah, mpox, chikungunya, Rift Valley fever, filoviruses and coronaviruses, vaccine manufacturing in the Global South, and the science and regulatory tools behind its 100 Days Mission (vaccines within 100 days of a new pandemic threat). About 86% of its money comes from governments; private donors give through donor-advised funds such as Fidelity Charitable.

spending.source: https://static.cepi.net/downloads/2026-04/CEPI%20Board%20of%20Directors'%20Report,%20Financial%20Statements%20and%20Auditors%20Report%202025.pdf (Board of Directors' Annual Report and Financial Statements 2025, p. 17, Profit & Loss, CEPI Group: total programme expenditure USD 428,226k of total expenditure USD 449,397k, calendar year 2025; audited)

lines.label: Vaccine research and development against priority pathogens and Disease X, manufacturing, enabling science, Global South partnerships and biosecurity, with programme support (every programme)
lines.source: https://static.cepi.net/downloads/2026-04/CEPI%20Board%20of%20Directors'%20Report,%20Financial%20Statements%20and%20Auditors%20Report%202025.pdf (p. 17: priority pathogens $196,715k, Disease X $61,276k, manufacturing $58,205k, enablers $37,321k, Global South partnerships $10,812k, biosecurity $795k, programme support $63,102k). One line because charityevals models them as one pandemic branch of one catastrophic-risk model, with the non-coronavirus priority pathogens' use against today's outbreaks as a second branch of the same model.
